summary: Milestone 2026.05.147 completed 14 experiments in 228.1 minutes, including 2 compute-bound experiments. The slowest compute-bound work was Exp 1880, which appears twice in the slowest list; GPU idle on compute-bound tasks is not flagged by the locked field.
bottlenecks_identified: Same-titled compute-bound Exp 1880 appears twice in the slowest list at 48.4 and 24.6 minutes, so compute-bound readiness and terminal-state handling need tighter gating.
The slowest single item was synthesis-only Exp 1877 at 52.7 minutes; this is wall-time pressure, but GPU idle is correct for synthesis-only work.
The retrospective closeout itself appears as synthesis-only Exp 1889 at 46.9 minutes, making artifact generation and documentation reconciliation a closeout bottleneck.
improvements_suggested: Record per-experiment GPU utilization spans, model_count, and parallel_model_count so GPU-idle claims are tied to active compute-bound windows instead of a single closeout snapshot.
Add same-title compute-bound terminal-state dedupe before relaunching a slow evaluation path.
Generate operational-retro JSON interpretation fields and docs append stubs directly from the locked timing artifact.
Add phase timing for synthesis-only work so long contract, bounds, and retrospective phases can be split or parallelized without treating GPU idle as a defect.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Add GPU/model-count telemetry and only flag DualGPURunner misses when parallel_model_count is at least 2.
Cache terminal compute-bound readiness outcomes before another same-title evaluation launch.
Automate the operational-retro JSON, changelog, and roadmap append path from the locked timing data.
meta_reflection: The estimate is intentionally conservative: it targets the repeated same-title compute-bound slow entry rather than assuming broad synthesis acceleration. No DualGPURunner failure is claimed because the supplied data does not show a compute-bound task with 2 or more models loaded in parallel.
